gramps-web-toolkit

gramps-web-toolkit is a set of command-line tools for running AI research agents against a family tree in [Gramps Web](https://www.grampsweb.org) without letting them write guesses into it. Each tool fixes a failure we hit while running about 30 research rounds over two trees of roughly 10,000 people each. The [pipeline design](docs/pipeline.md) and [every trap it taught us](docs/hard-won.md) sit next to the code. The toolkit works for genealogy in any country. One module, `spanish-poller`, is Spain-only: it watches the Spanish Ministry of Justice sede and the DEHú notification inbox. In `gwt-fetch`, `iiif` works with any IIIF archive, while `digibib`, `gazeta` and `geo` cover Spanish sources and `europeana` searches every provider in any country (`--provider Hispana` narrows it to Spain). ## Features - `gwt-apply`: applies a JSON Lines change list to a tree, reads before every write, skips what is already there, and stays dry-run until you pass `--apply` - `gwt-check`: reads the whole tree after an apply and reports orphans, dangling links, broken birth and death pointers, likely duplicates and what changed since the last copy, with a self-test that plants every error kind - `gwt-fetch`: downloads archive images and text without a browser, with one manifest row per file: any IIIF archive, Europeana search, plus Spanish sources (DIGIBIB, the historical Gaceta de Madrid, CartoCiudad geocoding) - `gwt-ledger`: a shared "already searched" ledger, so parallel agents stop repeating each other's negative searches - `gwt-fscache`: an on-disk HTTP cache for rate-limited genealogy APIs that never stores a block or an auth header - `gwt-gate`: one request pace shared by every agent on a machine, which backs off on a block and lets priority lanes go first - `gwt-rawstore`: keeps source images in an S3-compatible bucket and only a small manifest in git - `gwt-spanish-poller` (Spain only): watches Spanish civil-registry requests and the DEHú inbox read-only, and flags cases that vanish - `ocr-bench`: scores OCR, HTR and LLM readings of the same pages on how many names they recover ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/GeiserX/gramps-web-toolkit && cd gramps-web-toolkit python3 -m pip install -e apply # Python 3.11+, needs only requests gwt-apply changes.jsonl # dry-run: prints the plan and the diff ``` `gwt-check`, the ledger, cache and rawstore tools need only the Python standard library and run from their folders (`check/gwt-check`, `ledger/gwt-ledger`, `fscache/gwt-fscache`, `gate/gwt-gate`, `rawstore/gwt-rawstore`). `gwt-spanish-poller` needs Node 18+ and Playwright. ## Documentation - [The research pipeline](docs/pipeline.md): how agents, verifiers, a judge and a writer share one tree - [Hard-won lessons](docs/hard-won.md): each failure that cost us time, data or an account, and the rule that followed - [gwt-apply](docs/apply.md), [gwt-check](docs/check.md), [gwt-fetch](docs/fetch.md), [gwt-ledger](docs/ledger.md), [gwt-fscache](docs/fscache.md), [gwt-gate](docs/gate.md), [gwt-rawstore](docs/rawstore.md), [gwt-spanish-poller](docs/spanish-poller.md), [ocr-bench](docs/ocr-bench.md) ## License [GPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE)
